name: Forearm rotation (pronation / supination)
equipment: hammer or light dumbbell held at one end
summary: Elbow at 90° by the side, turn the palm up and then down with a hammer in the hand.
setup: Sit or stand with the elbow tucked and bent to 90°, holding a hammer near the head end. Turn the palm up until the hammer points sideways, then down the other way. Slow and controlled.
why: The forearm rotates on its own axis; the wrist barely changes position. Logged by hand.
progression: Hold the hammer lower on the handle.

faults.label: Elbow drifting away from the side
faults.cue: Keep the elbow at your side
faults.tip: Tuck a towel under the arm to keep the elbow still.

faults.label: Shoulder rotating
faults.tip: If the elbow swings in and out, the shoulder is turning instead.

faults.label: Bending the wrist
faults.tip: The rotation comes from the forearm bones, not from flicking the wrist.

faults.label: Half turns
faults.tip: Go to both ends of the turn; the stiffness usually lives at the very end.

points.t: Rotates fully palm up and palm down.
